name: Giant Snapping Turtle
pageNumbering: This copy counts the cover as page 1. The index is one greater than the printed folio.
sourceDistinctions: The book separately gives King Toba 120 HP and enhanced saving throws against magic on p. 83. Neither modifier belongs to the standard appendix creature.
Stable lists a DC 10 Dexterity check and all movement to stand without granting a different action economy.
The 2021 publisher errata has no alteration to this creature’s Appendix D stat block.
appearanceEvidence: Page 222 describes shells up to 12 ft. across and powerful snapping jaws. Shell scutes, beak details, and colors are editorial natural-history choices for the original portrait.
habitatEvidence: Appendix B encounter table p. 195 gives Beach, Rivers, and Swamp. Chapter 2 p. 36 identifies Snapping Turtle Bay.

name: Hadrosaurus
pageNumbering: This copy counts the cover as page 1. The index is one greater than the printed folio.
sourceDistinctions: The actual printed STR value is 15 (+2). OCR misreads it as −2. The printed Tail attack uses +4 to hit and 1d10 + 2.
The Racing Dinosaurs table in chapter 1 uses racetrack statistics. The encounter uses the appendix defaults.
The 2021 publisher errata has no alteration to this creature’s Appendix D stat block.
appearanceEvidence: The description on p. 224 specifies a bony head crest and semi-quadrupedal herbivore form. The crest contour and colors in the original are editorial.
habitatEvidence: Appendix B table p. 194 places hadrosauruses in jungle, river, and swamp encounters. The p. 197 encounter describes a grazing herd.

name: Jaculi
pageNumbering: This copy counts the cover as page 1. The index is one greater than the printed folio.
sourceDistinctions: Spring’s range and advantage threshold are distinct. The added damage follows a successful Spring Bite independent of the 10-ft. advantage threshold.
The 2021 publisher errata has no alteration to this creature’s Appendix D stat block.
appearanceEvidence: Appendix D p. 224 describes a 15-ft. snake whose scales imitate wood and stone. The credited plate on the same folio shows a cooler-toned spined head. The original portrait uses a different composition.
habitatEvidence: Appendix D p. 224 describes damp climates, rainforests, and cool dungeons. Appendix B p. 195 adds River and Ruins encounter categories.

name: Quetzalcoatlus
pageNumbering: This copy counts the cover as page 1. The index is one greater than the printed folio.
sourceDistinctions: The Dive Attack trait gives no separate damage type for the extra dice. The underlying Bite deals piercing damage.
The printed Bite targets one creature. The nearby Pterafolk belongs to another entry.
The 2021 publisher errata has no alteration to this creature’s Appendix D stat block.
appearanceEvidence: Page 229 describes a pteranodon relative with a wingspan over 30 ft. and a quadrupedal ground gait. Colors, crest and membrane anatomy are editorial pterosaur portrait choices.
habitatEvidence: Appendix B p. 194 places quetzalcoatluses in Beach, Mountains, and Rivers encounter columns. The p. 198 encounter describes a flight overhead.
